proposal_reality_cards.citizens_proposed: A higher minimum wage for adults (18+) with a separate, lower youth wage for teens.
proposal_reality_cards.lawmakers_tried: Nothing in this record. No 2019-2026 bill proposes a youth wage, training wage, or age bracket; 'youth wage' and 'training wage' return zero full-text hits. There is no state minimum wage to bracket, and Section 41-1-110 preempts local minimums.
proposal_reality_cards.where_similar_stopped: The parent idea (any state minimum wage) stops in first committee every time - 24 bills, zero votes.
proposal_reality_cards.levers_venue: State legislature; federal FLSA already allows a $4.25 youth training wage for the first 90 days, which a state bracket would interact with.
proposal_reality_cards.nearest_record: 124:S533 (Act 209 of 2022) enacted the opposite direction: it banned subminimum wages for workers with disabilities.
open_questions: Would a youth bracket attach to a new state minimum (never had a hearing) or stand alone?
Where would the age line sit, and does a lower teen wage displace adult workers?
How does an age tier square with the enacted policy direction of S533, which removed a subminimum tier?

proposal_reality_cards.citizens_proposed: Expand apprenticeships, career pathways, and technical-college training so workers can move into higher-paying jobs.
proposal_reality_cards.lawmakers_tried: The most active and most successful lane: SC WINS scholarships (124:H3144, Act 204 of 2022), workforce coordinating council (124:H4766, Act 194 of 2022), Earn and Learn (125:H3605, Act 13 of 2023), Statewide Education and Workforce Development Act (125:H3726, Act 67 of 2023), bigger apprentice tax credit (125:S557, Act 188 of 2024), STEM Opportunity Act (126:H3863, Act 142 of 2026) - all near-unanimous.
proposal_reality_cards.where_similar_stopped: The second chamber's committee late in the session: H3576 on the 2019-20 Senate calendar; H3759/S419 when COVID ended 2020; H4060 in Senate Education; S546/S279 and S859 in House committees.
proposal_reality_cards.levers_venue: State legislature plus the budget: apprenticeship lead-agency role, WINS lottery funding ($17M-$93.7M/yr), and workforce-needs funding all live in one-year budget provisos, not permanent statute.
open_questions: Is the remaining gap funding scale, employer take-up, or completion outcomes?
Which pieces should move from one-year provisos to permanent law?

proposal_reality_cards.citizens_proposed: Raise the state minimum wage toward a livable wage (mixed consensus; small-business cost concerns).
proposal_reality_cards.lawmakers_tried: 24 bills across all four sessions: fixed floors of $10-$17/hr, phased schedules with inflation adjustment, two advisory-referendum resolutions (124:S633, 125:S28), a constitutional amendment (123:S147), and a wage-board mechanism (126:H3735).
proposal_reality_cards.where_similar_stopped: First committee, every time, with no recorded vote at any stage in eight years.
proposal_reality_cards.levers_venue: State legislature only: the federal $7.25 floor applies, and Section 41-1-110 blocks cities and counties from setting their own minimums.
open_questions: What would earn the first committee hearing after 24 tries?
Is the advisory-referendum route a different path or the same chokepoint?
Does the small-business concern connect this proposal to the incentive design in [P-employer-living-wage-incentives]?

proposal_reality_cards.citizens_proposed: State incentives or bonuses for employers who pay a living wage (funding mechanism disputed).
proposal_reality_cards.lawmakers_tried: The exact design exists: 126:H4603, the Small Business Livable Wage Tax Credit Act (prefiled December 2025, introduced January 2026, led by Rep. Jones), died in House Ways and Means without a vote when the session ended. 126:H4245 (credits for hiring people leaving public assistance, also led by Rep. Jones) sits the same way; 124:S398 (wage obligations on subsidy recipients) died in Senate LCI.
proposal_reality_cards.where_similar_stopped: Stand-alone bills stop in the money committees without votes; wage-linked incentives pass when riding tax packages - 124:S901 (Act 237 of 2022) and 125:H4087 (Act 222 of 2024) updated job development credits near-unanimously, and 125:S557 grew the apprentice credit.
proposal_reality_cards.levers_venue: State tax code; the disputed funding question is in practice a House Ways and Means / Senate Finance question.
open_questions: How is 'livable wage' defined and updated, and is the credit refundable?
Does the design ride a committee tax package (the route that passes) or stand alone (the route that has not had a vote)?
What take-up would small employers actually see?

deliberation_prompts: If minimum-wage bills have stopped in the same first committees 24 times without a hearing, what would need to change for hearing number one?
Is a committee death a 'no' on the idea, or a 'no' on the vehicle? The Employment First bills died twice before S533 passed unanimously.
When a design keeps passing one chamber unanimously and dying in the other's committee (skills-based hiring, DEW restructuring), what does the second chamber need to see?
The one recorded floor defeat (H3368, overtime tax exemption, 16-27 in the Senate) followed a 121-0 House vote. What made the chambers read the same idea so differently?
Workforce-pathway laws pass almost unanimously. Does that mean the lane is open for more, or that the easy pieces are done?
Much of the apprenticeship and scholarship machinery lives in one-year budget provisos. Should any of it be permanent law, and who decides that?
A livable-wage tax credit exists as a filed bill that never got a vote. Is the obstacle the design, the definition of 'livable,' or the fiscal note?
No youth or training wage has ever been filed. Is that because no member has championed it, or because the parent policy has no traction?
